mechanism_narrative: A stable grocery-and-pharmacy series near baseline indicates resilient local demand that anchors retail footfall; as grocery stays above -5, retail-and-recreation rises over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is lower than over the last 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains above -5.0 throughout the two-week window.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL exceeds +8.5 and WORKPLACES falls below -8.0, work-from-home intensity suppresses weekday retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than over the last 7 days when both RESIDENTIAL >= +8.5 and WORKPLACES <= -8.0 hold.

mechanism_narrative: The joint recovery of PARKS and stabilization of TRANSIT generates leisure and errand trips that spill into retail; when both improve, RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days when PARKS > -12.0 and TRANSIT > -16.0 co-occur.

mechanism_narrative: In an endemic-reopening policy regime, grocery normalization below -3 reduces stockpiling and frees household time for discretionary retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
regime_hint: endemic reopening with no mobility restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM is at or above -3.0.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in WORKPLACES indicates growing remote-work adoption that reduces weekday commuting and nearby retail footfall, lowering RETAIL_REC over two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below -15.5, mobility avoidance signals reduced public-space activity that cuts retail trips, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than over the last 7 days when TRANSIT is at or below -15.5.
